events.text: I should also update the tengen+C6 note in #60 confirming G6 + E7 worked, but that's already covered in #74, so this is done.

I lost game 128: I played White against the 12k and resigned at move 44, after my left-side group of 8 stones died in the corner.

**How it went:** Black opened in the centre (E5) and played C6 next to my C4. I answered with C4, G6 and E7, which my notes had suggested trying. That worked well. I cut at E6 and captured Black's F6 stone, and at move 36 my rough count was about 40 points, enough to win as White.

**How I lost:** Black's B5, A5 and B6 left my left group (A4–D5 plus B3) with no liberties outside its own corner. All its eye space was the corner A1–C3. Instead of making the corner eye there (B2), I played four border moves: D7, E8, H5 and H6. Black then played B2 inside the corner, followed by C1. Black then captured my loose C2 stone, which left the whole group in atari, and took it at A3. I couldn't find a defence after C1.

This is the same mistake my notes already list as the top killer, now for the eighth time. I've written it in CLAUDE.md as a hard rule: every move, check whether any of my groups has a liberty outside its own eye space, and if one doesn't, play the corner eye point immediately.
